# Cross-language frame ring cases (AZ-3338). Each row is validated against the reference codec (framefmt.py) on load.
# seal <case> <key> <epoch> <dir> <tag_len> <msg_id> <kind> <ad> <clear> <plain> <expected_body> [<out_len>]
# mac <case> <key> <epoch> <label> <n> <message> <expected_tag>
# open <case> <key> <epoch> <dir> <tag_len> <msg_id> <kind> <ad> <clear_len> <body> <expected: TagMismatch|ShortPacket>
# verify <case> <key> <epoch> <label> <n> <message> <tag> invalid
# refuse-seal <case> <key> <epoch> <dir> <tag_len> <msg_id> <kind> <ad> <clear> <plain> <dirs> <out_len> <expected: BadValue|TooLong|BufferFull>
# refuse-open <case> <key> <epoch> <dir> <tag_len> <msg_id> <kind> <ad> <clear_len> <body> <dirs> <out_len> <expected>
# refuse-mac <case> <key> <epoch> <label> <n> <message> <expected: BadValue>
# dirs names the directions the session loaded (digits 1 to 3); out_len is the caller's output buffer. A refuse-seal and a
# refuse-mac row go to every writer once, a refuse-open row to every reader; each language must print the name (AZ-3354).
# The seal and mac rows after the worked examples, and the open and verify rows, were made with framefmt.py (AZ-3341);
# the loader derives every expected value again on each run, so a row that the reference does not confirm stops the ring.
# Hex fields have no separators; "-" is empty. epoch, dir, tag_len, kind, n, clear_len, out_len are decimal digits only, in
# the ranges of README.md (the loader stops on a number outside its range).
